Uploaded on December 18, 2022, the post shows Messi lifting his first World Cup Trophy after Argentina's win over France in the final. It is one of the most liked posts of all time across all social media platforms.
## History  
On January 4, 2019, the account @world_record_egg posted a photo of an egg with the specific purpose of surpassing the then most-liked Instagram post, a picture of Kylie Jenner's daughter with 18.6 million likes. The photo of the egg was originally taken by Serghei Platanov, who then posted it to Shutterstock on June 23, 2015, with the title "eggs isolated on white background." The creator of the @world_record_egg account was Chris Godfrey, an advertising creative, and his friends CJ Brown and Alissa Khan-Whelan.  
On January 14, 2019, the egg post became the most-liked post on Instagram, to which the egg's account owner wrote, "This is madness. What a time to be alive." Jenner responded with a video on Instagram of her cracking an egg open with the caption: "Take that little egg." Platanov was surprised by his photo's popularity, writing, "Egg is just an egg."  
On December 18, 2022, footballer Lionel Messi posted a carousel with photos of him lifting the FIFA World Cup Trophy and celebrating with his teammates after winning the 2022 FIFA World Cup with Argentina, which reached 10 million likes within the first 39 minutes of its sharing. The following day, the post became the most-liked Instagram post in the first 24 hours of its sharing, with 50 million likes. On December 20, 2022, the post reached over 56 million likes, surpassing the previous record held by @world_record_egg.
Within 48 hours of Messi posting, the Instagram post had surpassed 64 million likes, and in doing so, it became the most-liked social media post ever across all social media platforms, by overtaking the most-liked post on YouTube, the music video for the song "Despacito", which had reached 50.2 million likes, and the most-liked post on TikTok, a video uploaded by Bella Poarch featuring her lip-syncing to the song "Sophie Aspin Send", which had reached 60.3 million likes. This also meant that it became the first ever post on Instagram to reach 60 and 70 million likes, achieving that in just 3 days since it was posted.

Instagram – the platform that popularized the phenomenon of racking up followers and likes on posts as a form of social approval. Depending on who you ask, hundreds of likes may seem like a lot; to some, thousands rather. But as the platform has grown to over 2 billion users, we’ve entered the era of posts receiving millions upon millions of likes, and competition for having the most-liked post ever. Welcome to an exploration of Instagram's most popular post, a digital marvel that has captivated millions. In this article, we’ll answer the question of what is the most liked Instagram post, as well as explore other posts that have captured the attention of millions of Instagram users along the way.
## **The start of the “most-liked Instagram post ever” trend**  
The egg post that previously held the record for the most-liked Instagram post in history was published on January 4, 2019, by the account @world\_record\_egg. The post featured a photo of a single, ordinary-looking egg with the caption "Let's set a world record together and get the most liked post on Instagram. Beating the current world record held by Kylie Jenner (18 million)! We got this." The post quickly went viral and became a global phenomenon, with people from all over the world liking and sharing the post in an attempt to break the record.  
The egg post gained attention for its simplicity and absurdity, as well as the challenge it presented to beat the previous record held by Kylie Jenner. It also sparked a humorous social media competition between fans of the egg and fans of Jenner, with both sides trying to outdo each other in terms of likes. The egg ultimately achieved its goal, surpassing Jenner's record and becoming the most-liked post on Instagram with 18.4 million likes. The account behind the egg post later revealed that it was created as a social media experiment by an anonymous group of friends in an attempt to see how far they could spread positivity through social media.
### **Selena Gomez (@selenagomez):**  
Selena, a widely recognized American singer, actress, and producer, has built an impressive presence on Instagram with over 418 million followers. As such, she has established herself as one of the platform's most prominent figures. As the most-followed woman on Instagram, overtaking Kylie Jenner and others in the Kardashian clan, Selena has no shortage of popular Instagram posts, with her most-liked being a recent selfie with the caption “Violet Chemistry”.
